title: Entering Türkiye: Visa-Free Stays, e-Visas and the 90/180 Rule
excerpt: Whether you need a visa, how the 90/180 rule counts your days, e-Visa pitfalls, passport validity, the Digital Nomad route, staying longer, and what overstaying costs.
bodyHtml:
Before travelling to Türkiye, check three things: whether your passport requires a visa, how long you are allowed to stay, and whether your passport has enough validity remaining. These requirements depend on your nationality, passport type and reason for travelling.

Entry and residence rules can change. This guide is practical information, not legal or immigration advice — check the linked official sources before acting.

Check your passport first

Start with the Ministry of Foreign Affairs’ country-by-country visa guidance. Depending on your circumstances, you may qualify for visa-free entry, an online e-Visa, or a visa issued through a Turkish embassy or consulate. Visa on arrival remains available in some cases, but you should confirm your eligibility before departure.

The 90/180 rule

The 90/180 rule counts your visits together. For many visitors, the allowance is up to 90 days within any 180-day period. Some nationalities have shorter per-visit limits or additional restrictions.

This is a rolling calculation. Earlier visits can still count towards your allowance when you return. A short trip outside Türkiye does not automatically give you another 90 days, and switching between two passports does not create a second allowance. Keep a record of your entry and exit dates and check both your nationality’s rules and the conditions of any visa issued to you. Official guidance on stay limits.

The e-Visa

Apply for an e-Visa through the official e-Visa portal — only there. Third-party websites may charge extra fees and do not act for the Government of Türkiye. Eligibility and conditions depend on your travel document. Some applicants must also hold a qualifying visa or residence permit from a Schengen country, the United States, the United Kingdom or Ireland, and may face additional requirements. Check every condition shown for your application. MFA visa guidance.

When applying:

  • Allow time before departure. The official recommendation is to apply at least 48 hours before travelling; this is a recommended lead time, rather than a mandatory waiting period. Application timing.

  • Check your personal and passport details carefully. An e-Visa with information that does not match your travel document is invalid. Passport-detail requirements.

  • Save a copy on your phone or carry a printout. Border officers can check the visa electronically, but the government recommends keeping a copy available. Holding an e-Visa does not guarantee admission. Official e-Visa guidance.

Your visa’s validity dates, permitted length of stay and number of entries are separate limits. Check all three before booking your trip.

A changed arrival date does not always require another e-Visa. You can arrive on a different date within the visa’s existing validity window, provided you still meet its entry and stay conditions. If you need to change the validity dates themselves, the system does not amend them: you must obtain another e-Visa. Arrival-date rules, date amendments.

Passport validity

Check passport validity against your permitted stay. The general requirement is at least 60 days of passport validity beyond the authorised duration of your visa or visa exemption. For a 90-day allowance, that means at least 150 days of validity when you enter.

The Ministry of Foreign Affairs separately recommends having at least six months’ validity from arrival. Exceptions exist for certain national-ID arrangements, recognised expired passports and diplomatic, special or official passports. Check the exception that applies to your actual document before relying on it. Official passport requirements.

Work, study and remote work

For work or study, confirm the appropriate route before travelling. An e-Visa is issued for tourism or commerce. Employment generally requires separate work authorisation. Study requirements vary: certain students covered by university, exchange or educational programmes can enter visa-free and apply for student residence without first obtaining a student visa. Confirm your circumstances with the Turkish mission and, for study, your university. MFA guidance on visa purposes and student exceptions.

Türkiye also has an official Digital Nomad programme. Its published identification-certificate requirements include:

  • Citizenship of an eligible country and an age between 21 and 55.

  • A university diploma or another document proving university graduation.

  • An employment contract with a company outside Türkiye, or, for self-employed applicants, a business contract with a company outside Türkiye.

  • Evidence of income of at least US$3,000 per month or US$36,000 per year.

  • A passport valid for at least six months from arrival.

  • A biometric photograph.

The first step is obtaining a Digital Nomad Identification Certificate. You then use the certificate and the other required documents to apply for the visa through a Turkish visa centre or consulate. The certificate itself is not the visa. Official programme requirements.

YİMER states that people whose Digital Nomad visa applications are approved may, after entering Türkiye and during their visa period, apply through e-İkamet for a six-month tourism-based short-term residence permit. This is an application route, not a guarantee of approval. YİMER’s Turkish FAQ.

Staying longer

If you want to stay longer, apply before your lawful stay expires. Use the official e-İkamet system to apply for a residence-permit category whose requirements you meet. Complete the online application while your stay is still lawful, then follow the appointment and document instructions. YİMER application guidance.

For a standard first application, the process includes an appointment with the migration authority and submission of the required documents. Applying does not guarantee approval. Residence-permit information. Our residence permit guide walks through a first application.

You cannot apply for a new e-Visa from inside Türkiye once your e-Visa has expired. Leaving may be necessary before another application, but it does not reset the 90/180 limit.

If you overstay

Overstaying can result in fines, removal and an entry ban. Overstaying a visa or visa-exemption period by more than ten days is a statutory ground for a removal decision, subject to legal exceptions. This threshold should not be treated as permission to stay ten extra days. Official removal guidance.

The Migration Management entry-ban notice dated 9 June 2020 sets out the following periods for people who voluntarily leave before their overstay is detected and pay the applicable administrative fine:

  • Less than 3 months: no entry ban under this provision

  • 3–6 months: 1 month

  • 6 months–1 year: 3 months

  • 1–2 years: 1 year

  • 2–3 years: 2 years

  • More than 3 years: 5 years

Different rules apply in other circumstances, including unpaid fines and certain removal or conditional-entry cases. Outstanding fines or other public debts can also prevent entry after a ban has expired. Official entry-ban notice.

If your dates are close to the limit or you think you have overstayed, get case-specific guidance from the Turkish authorities or a qualified immigration lawyer before making travel plans.
